# `modules/EntitySchema.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/modules/EntitySchema.js`

EntitySchema - JSON Schema system for entity serialization and relationship tracking Captures: - All entity properties and components - Parent/child relationships - References to other entities - Physics bodies, colliders, joints - Attached emitters, scripts, etc.

## Functions

### `generateEntitySchema(editor, entityId)`

Generate a full JSON schema for an entity

**Parameters:**

- `editor` *(Object)* — Editor instance
- `entityId` *(number)* — Entity ID

**Returns:** Complete entity schema

### `generateSceneSchema(editor)`

Generate schemas for all entities in the scene

**Parameters:**

- `editor` *(Object)* — Editor instance

**Returns:** Scene schema with all entities

### `exportSceneToJSON(editor, pretty = true)`

Export scene schema to JSON string

### `debugEntitySchema(editor, entityId)`

Print entity schema to console (for debugging)

### `debugSceneSchema(editor)`

Print full scene schema to console (for debugging)

### `getRelationshipSummary(editor, entityId)`

Get a summary of entity relationships

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```
